title: Visualize the tense meeting first
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What will you feel in the meeting if you miss the deadline?
Jose asked a student: what motivates you on a Monday, what do you say to yourself? He said you are putting triggers all over the place, emotional, visual and others.
A student said that it is hard because you are used to things and too comfortable, so when you change you have to hack yourself.

Jose asked a student to give an example of something he would do today and visualize it before it happens: logging on, a client looking for guidance, a meeting room with a glass table where people file in.
He asked: how are you feeling going into that meeting because you did not hit the task? The effects could be negativity: if we did not get this up, we lost sales.
He said you want to be so comfortable visualizing the objections, the challenges, the obstacles and the aggression on the other side that none of it throws you.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a hard meeting this week.
Write the room, the people and what they say.
Write the objection you fear most.
Write how you will feel afterwards.

check.q: What did Jose ask a student to do?
What did Jose say to be comfortable with?
choices: Objections and aggression on the other side

check.q: What did a student say you have to do to change?

recap: Visualize the hard meeting until nothing in it throws you.
